why: Most commands are fine. The builder's printf/node pipelines, the JS test strings ('[{"a\\tb":"1\\t2"}]\n' gives a literal backslash-t), `npm test`, the grep, and verifier Checks 1–4 and 6 all run correctly as written. Check 5 does not. In `printf '[{"a\\\\tb":"1\\\\t2"}]\n' > /tmp/c5.exp`, the single quotes pass four backslashes to printf, which turns them into two. The expected file then holds `a\\tb`, not `a\tb`, so `cmp` would report a difference even against a correct implementation. The brief admits its escaping may be wrong and offers a node fallback that does work. Still, the primary command, as written, does not produce what it claims, so not every command runs as written.
